subject: Math
prompt: Data set A consists of the masses of $60$ rocks and has a mean of $28$ grams. Data set B consists of the masses of $90$ rocks and has a mean of $58$ grams. Data set C consists of the masses of the $150$ rocks from data sets A and B. What is the mean, in grams, of data set C?
explanation: The correct answer is $46$. The mean of a data set is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. For data set A, the sum of the masses is $60 \times 28 = 1{,}680$ grams. For data set B, the sum of the masses is $90 \times 58 = 5{,}220$ grams. Data set C combines all $150$ rocks, so its mean is $\frac{1{,}680 + 5{,}220}{150} = \frac{6{,}900}{150} = 46$ grams. Therefore, the mean of data set C is $46$ grams.
